recheck.why: Lint is 1.000 and clean, the DV content is technically correct throughout (auto_bin_max 64 / 64^3=262144, Amdahl 2/5 -> ~1.7x, the uvm_info verbosity guard, global time precision, associative vs packed allocation, CPU:wall read both ways), all seven slots are spent, role/level are applications-engineer/staff, 260 lines, and no handoff field collides with a T1 enum or a T3 held noun. But it ships two dangling cross-references of exactly the class standing rule 8 names: it calls dv-compute-license-efficiency's slot "Cost columns" when that skill names it "Cost and status columns" (dv-compute-license-efficiency/SKILL.md:45), and it calls dv-regression-tiering-farm's slot "Resource request" when that skill names it "Job resource and retry" (dv-regression-tiering-farm/SKILL.md:48). Each is wrong in two places and each is load-bearing inside the Procedure (line 190 tells the agent to Grep for what "Cost columns" names; line 111 routes a killed run to "Resource request"), so a reader who follows the pointer finds no such slot. On top of that the budget does not account for every Grep step 7 actually spends: rule 4 prices an iteration at two Greps and one Read "of the new log" while the step asks for the path of EACH resulting log and demands the ratio beat the band over the repeats the band was measured across, so the real cost is 2N Greps and N Reads per iteration with N unbounded. I would not hand this to a working DV engineer today.
remaining: BLOCKER — wrong sibling slot name, twice: lines 59 and 190 say `dv-compute-license-efficiency`'s **Cost columns**. That skill's slot is **Cost and status columns** (skills/dv-compute-license-efficiency/SKILL.md:45). Line 190 is a Procedure step that instructs a Grep for 'the resource columns dv-compute-license-efficiency's Cost columns names' — a step depending on a slot nobody defined.

BLOCKER — wrong sibling slot name, twice: lines 59 and 111 say `dv-regression-tiering-farm`'s **Resource request**. That skill has no such slot; the fact ('the memory, wall clock and queue one job asks for by default, what the scheduler does when a job exceeds one of them') lives under **Job resource and retry** (skills/dv-regression-tiering-farm/SKILL.md:48). Line 111 is the Procedure's routing step for a run killed rather than slowed.

Undeclared narrowing: line 58-59 asserts identity ('are') between 'the summary's wall clock, CPU time, cores and memory columns' and the sibling slot, but that slot is strictly wider — it also asks 'what its status column writes for a job killed at a wallclock or memory limit'. Standing rule 8 requires saying exactly how it is narrower.

Budget under-counts step 7: rule 4 prices each tuning iteration at 'two Greps and one 60-line Read of the new log', but step 7 asks for 'the path of each resulting log' and requires the ratio to beat the Noise band 'over the repeats that band was measured across'. With a band measured over N runs an iteration costs 2N Greps and N Reads; the five-iteration stopping rule bounds iterations, not logs, so nothing bounds the Grep count.

`run id` has no budgeted retrieval. Step 1's single Grep alternates only the Stage markers with the Resource summary line and the text says it is 'the only Grep this step gets', yet the same step must 'read the run's identity off it' via the profile's Run identity fact, and the verification section forbids taking it from the log's file name. Either add the Run identity string to that Grep's alternation or budget a call for it.

Baseline repeat count is never obtainable. The `speedup` field asks 'how many runs each number rests on' and Human verification requires 'the repeat count behind each number is stated', but only the tuned side gets repeats — the baseline is the one log from step 1, which the skill's own rule ('One run against one on a shared farm is not a measurement') then rejects.
